digest.component_or_area: reconciler committed state cache and tickets repository storage
propositions: The tickets branch is 1.04 GiB, of which 92% is the reconciler's .bridge_state cache; the actual ticket events are only 55 MB, indicating bookkeeping overhead defeating git delta compression.

Diffing consecutive bindings.json revisions shows 1144 changes per pass to baseline_advanced_at (written but never read in src/) and 20 changes to last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping; deleting the timestamp alone reduces marginal cost by 7.4x (12.79 KB to 1.74 KB per version).

The reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners so durable state must live in git, making the cache location fixed; the solution is to reduce content churn and committed-format footprint, not relocate the cache.

A git fast-export/filter/fast-import pipeline on real history proved capable of reducing 1.17 GB to 98.8 MB (8.4%) while preserving all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges and producing byte-identical HEAD tree after dynamic re-add of current files.

Rollout requires gated descendant-workflow execution, live epoch-mismatch refusal probes from review-bot and host runtimes, quiesced writer windows, verified off-repo backup bundle, and operator attestation before reclaim publication; rollback is an explicit second quiesced procedure.

Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state must produce byte-identical bindings.json and create no commit; text-normalized baseline and key-set-narrowed prev_snapshot must produce zero delta in non-empty Jira effects.
